units.name: UNIT - V (Reading Comprehension)
units.passage:
The world's coral reefs, vibrant underwater ecosystems, are facing an unprecedented crisis due to climate change. Rising ocean temperatures are causing coral bleaching, a phenomenon where corals expel the algae that give them colour and nutrients. Prolonged coral bleaching can lead to coral death, devastating the diverse marine life that depend on these reefs for survival. Scientists warn that if current trends continue, a significant portion of the world's coral reefs could disappear within decades. This loss would have catastrophic consequences, impacting fisheries, tourism and coastal protection. Beyond warming waters, other threats to coral reefs include pollution, overfishing, and destructive fishing practices.
Conservation efforts are crucial to protect these invaluable ecosystems. Researchers are working on developing more resilient coral species and implementing measures to reduce local stressors. However, the most critical step is to address climate change by reducing green-house gas emissions. The fate of coral reefs rests on our ability to take swift and decisive action to mitigate the impacts of global warming.
